specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) spatial search on a graph, analysed by reducing the dynamics to a small invariant (Krylov) subspace generated by the Lanczos algorithm from the marked vertex; the abstract claims this yields new optimal-search instances including complete graphs with broken links and complete bipartite graphs (star graph).
specification.reconstruction_scope: ONE smallest useful construction chosen (no experiment_scope supplied): CTQW spatial search on the star graph K_{1,N-1} with the marked vertex being a leaf, reduced via Lanczos from |w> to a 3-dimensional invariant subspace, with a tiny explicit instance N=4 (center vertex 0, leaves 1,2,3, marked vertex w=1) encoded on 2 qubits. Outside scope: complete graphs with broken links, general complete bipartite graphs K_{m,n}, quantum transport efficiency calculations, link-removal efficiency improvements, and the XY spin-network single-qubit transfer fidelity bound. The paper's specific choice of Hamiltonian (adjacency vs Laplacian), optimal hopping rate gamma and search time are not stated in the abstract and are treated as assumptions/missing.

symbols.meaning: Undirected graph on which the walk takes place; here the star graph K_{1,N-1}
Number of vertices (Hilbert space dimension of the walker)
Adjacency matrix of G, A_{uv}=1 iff (u,v) in E

symbols.domain: computational basis state of the vertex register; instance w=1

symbols.meaning: Center vertex state of the star graph
Normalised uniform superposition over unmarked leaves
Uniform superposition over all vertices (initial state)
Search Hamiltonian restricted to the Lanczos invariant subspace
Success probability of measuring the marked vertex at time t

equations.label: CTQW spatial search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard Childs–Goldstone continuous-time spatial search Hamiltonian with adjacency-matrix walk term and marked-vertex oracle term.
equations.justification: The abstract names the spatial quantum search algorithm but gives no formula; this is the standard CTQW search Hamiltonian. Whether the paper uses the adjacency matrix or the Laplacian is not stated.
assumptions: Adjacency matrix (not Laplacian) is used for the walk term

equations.label: Initial uniform state
equations.description: Walker starts in the equal superposition over all N vertices.
equations.justification: Standard initial state of CTQW spatial search.

equations.label: Lanczos recursion generating the invariant subspace
equations.description: Three-term Lanczos recursion started from the marked vertex; termination (vanishing beta) yields an H-invariant Krylov subspace in which H is tridiagonal.
equations.abstract_quote: we use invariant subspace methods, that can be computed systematically using Lanczos algorithm, to obtain the reduced set of states that encompass the dynamics of the problem at hand without the specific knowledge of underlying symmetries
equations.justification: The abstract states the invariant subspace is computed with the Lanczos algorithm; the recursion itself is the standard Lanczos iteration. Starting vector |w> is an assumption (the exact Hamiltonian/starting vector used in the paper is not given).
assumptions: Lanczos is seeded with |w> and applied to the search Hamiltonian H (or equivalently to A, since |w><w| preserves the Krylov space of A seeded at |w>)

equations.label: Reduced basis for the star graph with a marked leaf
equations.description: Lanczos from |w> on the star graph terminates after three vectors; the initial state |s> lies in this subspace, so the full dynamics is confined to it.
equations.justification: Proposed concrete realisation of the reduction for the star graph (abstract: 'complete bipartite graphs, in particular, the star graph'); follows from A|w>=|c> and A|c>=|w>+sqrt(N-2)|r>, but the paper's specific reduced basis is not quoted in the abstract.
assumptions: Marked vertex is a leaf, not the center
N >= 3 so that |r> is well defined

equations.label: Reduced search Hamiltonian in basis (|w>,|c>,|r>)
equations.description: Exact (not approximate) 3x3 restriction of H to the invariant subspace of eq_4; dynamics of |s> under H equals dynamics of its 3-component coordinate vector under H_red.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_1 and eq_4 for the star graph under the stated assumptions; not a relation quoted from the abstract.

equations.label: Success probability and optimality criterion
equations.description: Probability of finding the marked vertex after time t; search is called optimal if a constant success probability is reached in time scaling as sqrt(N).
equations.abstract_quote: new instances of graphs where the spatial quantum search algorithm is optimal: complete graphs with broken links and complete bipartite graphs, in particular, the star graph
equations.justification: The abstract claims optimality of spatial search on the star graph; 'optimal' is interpreted in the standard sense of Grover-like O(sqrt N) time with Theta(1) success probability. The specific values of gamma and t* for the star graph are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Standard definition of optimal spatial search

registers.name: vertex
registers.size: n = log2(N) qubits; 2 qubits for the N=4 instance
registers.role: Encodes the walker position; vertex index v in {0,...,N-1} stored in binary (big-endian: qubit 0 is the most significant bit). Vertex 0 is the star center, vertices 1..N-1 are leaves, marked vertex w=1.

specification.initial_state: |s> = H^{\otimes 2}|00> = (1/2)(|0>+|1>+|2>+|3>) on the 2-qubit vertex register (eq_2), equal to (1/2)(|w>+|c>+sqrt(2)|r>) in the reduced basis for N=4.

steps.description: Classical preprocessing: build A for the star graph K_{1,N-1}, form H (eq_1), run Lanczos from |w> (eq_3) to obtain the 3-dimensional invariant basis (eq_4) and H_red (eq_5); choose gamma and evolution time t* by maximising p(t) from eq_6 using the 3x3 matrix (values not supplied by the abstract).
Prepare the uniform superposition over vertices with Hadamards on every qubit of the vertex register.

Apply the unitary U(t*) = exp(-i H t*) on the vertex register (for N=4 this is a 4x4 unitary that can be compiled exactly; for larger N a Trotter approximation of exp(i gamma A t) and exp(i |w><w| t) would introduce approximation error).
Measure the vertex register in the computational basis and record whether the outcome equals w.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of all vertex-register qubits; outcome bit string decoded as integer v; success iff v = w (=1, i.e. bit string 01 for N=4).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate p(t*) as the fraction of shots yielding v=w; compare to the exact value obtained from exp(-i H_red t*) (eq_6) to validate the reduced-subspace prediction.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the star graph with a marked leaf and N=4 was chosen as the single smallest useful instance
Search Hamiltonian uses the adjacency matrix with a projector oracle (eq_1); the paper may instead use the graph Laplacian
Marked vertex is a leaf; marking the center gives a different (2-dimensional) reduction
gamma and t* are to be determined numerically from H_red; no paper values are available from the abstract
Exact unitary synthesis of exp(-iHt) for the 4x4 instance; Trotterisation is not analysed
missing_information: Exact form of the search Hamiltonian used in the paper (adjacency vs Laplacian, sign conventions)
Paper's optimal hopping rate gamma and search time for the star graph and complete bipartite graphs
Paper's treatment of complete graphs with broken links (which links are removed, resulting reduced subspace)
Definition and formulas for the quantum transport efficiency and the link-removal results
XY spin-network Hamiltonian and the derivation of the upper bound on single-qubit transfer fidelity
Whether the paper's Lanczos reduction is seeded from the marked vertex, the initial state, or another vector
